tasks.prompt: Inspect the business workspace and report what is there. Do not modify any file.
In project/config.json change only the format field from html to markdown. Do not change any other value.
Run project/broken.py, diagnose the failure, fix it with the smallest reasonable change, and run it again successfully.
Analyze business/sales.csv and identify the most important anomaly. Explain which records support your conclusion.
Read the business notes and produce a concise list of the reporting rules that must be respected.
Using the business CSV files and notes, produce a concise executive summary for August. Do not modify source CSV files.
Remember these workflow preferences for future sessions: use Python for small tools; do not commit Git changes without asking; keep generated reports under reports/. Do not change files now.
Without being given the previous instructions, state the three workflow preferences you should apply to this task.
Update the stored preference: for data-analysis tools, prefer TypeScript instead of Python. Keep the other preferences unchanged.
Create a repeatable workflow for generating the monthly business report from the provided CSV files and notes. After completing it, record what you learned so it can be reused.
Generate the monthly business report again using the workflow you learned previously. Use the learned procedure rather than rediscovering it from scratch.
The previous monthly-report workflow missed unusually large transactions. Improve the reusable workflow so future reports explicitly flag outliers, then run it on the current data.
Create a small Python CLI at project/csv_summary.py that reads a CSV path and prints row count and numeric total for the amount column. Include a --help option.
Create tests for project/csv_summary.py covering an empty CSV, normal values, and a malformed amount value. Run the tests.
Refactor project/csv_summary.py for clarity without changing its CLI behavior. Run its tests after the refactor.

Create an August expense report from the business workspace. Decide yourself which files are relevant, calculate totals, flag unusual expenses, and save the report under business/reports/. Do not alter source data.
Read business/README.md and answer the question it enables you to answer. Do not inspect unrelated project files or run commands unless necessary.
Produce a report from the business data even if one intermediate approach fails. Recover from errors without asking the user unless a destructive or ambiguous action is required.
Research one current public fact relevant to local AI agents, cite the source URL, and save a short markdown note at research/current-agent-fact.md. Do not use private credentials.
Find three current public sources about local LLM agent tooling and save a comparison table with title, URL, date accessed, and one-sentence takeaway at research/agent-tools.md.

End-to-end task: inspect the business workspace, identify the relevant data, create a monthly report, validate the result, and leave a short changelog in business/reports/CHANGELOG.md. Never modify source CSVs.
Build the small CSV summary tool, write tests, run them, fix any failures, and leave the project in a working state. Keep changes limited to project/.
Complete the monthly report task, record one genuinely useful lesson from the execution, and on the next run apply that lesson without being reminded.

Complete the business report task with no unnecessary user questions. Ask only if a decision is genuinely ambiguous or potentially destructive. Record the final artifact and a concise activity summary.
